title_en: Foshan Shunde Taibao Investment Management Co., Ltd. v. Guangdong Zhongding Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over contract for assignment of creditor's rights
ruling_gist_en: A creditor who assigns a right shall notify the debtor. If no notice is given, the assignment shall not be effective against the debtor, and the debtor shall have the right to raise a defense against the assignee, but this shall not affect the validity of the assignment agreement between the assignor and the assignee.
keywords_en: Civil; dispute over contract for assignment of creditor's rights; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Guangdong Province; legal person; Contract Law; effectiveness of notice of assignment of creditor's rights; validity of assignment agreement and debtor's defense right; affirm the original judgment; assignment of creditor's rights; notice to debtor; right of defense; contract dispute; dispute over assignment of creditor's rights by a limited company
full_text_en:
Foshan Shunde Taibao Investment Management Co., Ltd. v. Guangdong Zhongding Group Co., Ltd.

— Dispute over Debt Transfer Contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where a creditor transfers its rights, it shall notify the debtor. If no notice is given, such transfer shall not be effective against the debtor, and the debtor is entitled to the defense right against the transferee. However, this does not affect the validity of the debt transfer agreement between the transferor and the transferee.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 212

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Foshan Shunde Taibao Investment Management Co., Ltd. Address: No. 102 Dafu Building, Hongqi Road, Ronggui Street, Shunde District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Hu Guoying, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Xinbo, attorney at Beijing Yifeng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Chunming, attorney at Guangdong Guang Kai Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Guangdong Zhongding Group Co., Ltd. Address: Second Floor, No. 73 Nan'an Road, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Tan Liming, Chairperson of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wu Jianyun, attorney at Beijing Shouxin Law Firm.

The Appellant, Foshan Shunde Taibao Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taibao Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2004) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 6 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court in the case of dispute over a debt transfer contract with the Respondent, Guangdong Zhongding Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongding Company). This Court formed a collegial panel composed of trial judges Zhang Yongjian, Wang Dongmin, and acting trial judge Yin Yuan to hear the case, with Zhang Yongjian serving as the presiding judge and Zhang Yongshu serving as the court clerk. The case has now been concluded.

The Guangdong High People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

On November 25, 2002, Zhongding Company and the China Oriental Asset Management Corporation Guangzhou Office (hereinafter referred to as the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office) entered into a "Debt Transfer Agreement," stipulating: 1. The Oriental Company Guangzhou Office transferred to Zhongding Company debts totaling over RMB 4.4 billion, including the debt involved in this case, with a total transfer price of RMB 318,622,497. The payment method was divided into four installments. Upon payment of the first installment of RMB 165,683,698.8, Zhongding Company was to pay the remaining amount in three equal installments to the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office within the period from December 29, 2002, to December 28, 2003: RMB 31,862,249.77 before March 18, 2003; RMB 60,538,274.56 before June 18, 2003; and RMB 60,538,274.56 before September 18, 2003. 2. The conditions precedent for the effectiveness of the agreement were: the authorized representatives of both parties signed and sealed the agreement, and Zhongding Company satisfied all the conditions precedent listed in the contract, only then would the subject debts be transferred from the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office to Zhongding Company. The conditions precedent were: (1) Zhongding Company must pay the full first installment of RMB 165,683,698.8 to the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office within one month from the date of signing the contract; (2) Zhongding Company must enter into a "Management Service Provider and Fund Account Supervision Agreement" with the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office and the management service provider, and such agreement must have legally taken effect; (3) Zhongding Company must sign a "Debt Pledge Contract" with the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office, pledging the subject debts to the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office immediately after the transfer as security for the repayment of the transfer price, and issue a notice to the borrowers and guarantors regarding the pledge of the subject debts (including their ancillary security interests) to the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office; (4) The "Joint Liability Guarantee Contract" signed between the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office and Yangjiang Municipal Machinery Road Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. must have legally taken effect; (5) The Oriental Company Guangzhou Office must have signed a "Service and Assistance Agreement" and a "Preemptive Right and Repurchase Option Agreement" with Zhongding Company. 3. After the conditions precedent of the contract were satisfied and the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office transferred the subject debts to Zhongding Company, both parties were to jointly issue a notice to the borrowers and guarantors by notarial service, informing the borrowers and guarantors in writing of the change in the obligee of the subject debts. Whether the borrowers or any guarantor signed and confirmed receipt of the notice would not affect the validity of the debt transfer under this agreement, nor the validity of the transfer of the security interests attached to the subject debts along with the subject debts. 4. Regarding the retransfer of the subject debts: Zhongding Company could retransfer all or any part of the subject debts to a third party only if all of the following conditions were satisfied: (1) During the three-year cooperation period and at the expiration of the cooperation, if the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office did not have a preemptive right over the subject debts that Zhongding Company intended to transfer in accordance with the "Preemptive Right and Repurchase Option Agreement," or if the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office had such a right but waived its exercise; (2) The proceeds from the transfer must be fully deposited into the supervision account; (3) In the transfer contract, the new proposed transferee must make declarations and warranties identical in content to those in Clause 9.2.7 of this contract; (4) If Zhongding Company intended to transfer any part or all of the subject debts to an overseas investor, prior consent from the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office must be obtained. Clause 9.2.7 provided: Zhongding Company acknowledges the corporate legal person enterprise system established by the laws of the People's Republic of China and the enterprise legal person status of the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office, fully understands and recognizes that the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office did not originally have any form of claim right against the state or government of the People's Republic of China based on the subject debts, and guarantees that it will not acquire any such claim right as a result of the transfer of the subject debts; Zhongding Company will only initiate litigation or arbitration against the borrowers and/or guarantors of the subject debts within the territory of the People's Republic of China in accordance with the laws of the People's Republic of China; in special circumstances, if the borrowers and/or guarantors have assets outside China, Zhongding Company may initiate litigation or arbitration in Hong Kong in accordance with Hong Kong law. Zhongding Company also hereby undertakes: if it subsequently transfers its contractual rights and interests under this contract in accordance with the relevant provisions of Article 15 of this contract, or retransfers all or part of the subject debts to any third party, Zhongding Company will ensure that such transferee makes the same commitments; otherwise, any disputes or liabilities arising therefrom shall be borne solely by Zhongding Company. And so on.

On the same day of signing the above "Debt Transfer Agreement," the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office and Zhongding Company also entered into the "Management Service Provider and Fund Account Supervision Agreement," "Debt Pledge Contract," "Joint Liability Guarantee Contract," "Service and Assistance Agreement," and "Preemptive Right and Repurchase Option Agreement" as stipulated in the conditions precedent. Thereafter, Zhongding Company paid the first installment of RMB 125,683,698.8 to the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office. The deposit of RMB 3 million paid by Zhongding Company on October 31, 2002, and the deposit of RMB 37 million paid on November 11, 2002, were also converted into the first installment. Zhongding Company paid a total of RMB 165,683,698.8 to the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office.

In January 2003, Zhongding Company issued a "Preemptive Purchase Notice" to the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office, stating: Zhongding Company intends to transfer to Taibao Company the debt of Guizhou Construction Comprehensive Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Guizhou Company) in the principal amount of RMB 114,187,454.22 and corresponding interest, with a transfer price of RMB 75 million, to be paid in full by July 27, 2003. Considering that the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office has a preemptive right to purchase, your company may preemptively purchase at the above price and payment terms, and shall reply in writing within five working days of receiving this notice. On January 23 of the same month, the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office signed for receipt of the notice.

On January 29, 2003, Zhongding Company and Taibao Company entered into a "Debt Transfer Agreement," stipulating: 1. Pursuant to the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed by Zhongding Company and the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office on November 25, 2002, Zhongding Company acquired from the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office the relevant debts in the Shunde area transferred from the Bank of China and the security interests under such debts, including the debt of Guizhou Company in the principal amounts of RMB 114,187,454.22 and USD 5,386,034.31 and corresponding interest. Through negotiation and in accordance with the rules and procedures agreed with the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office, legal recognition was obtained, and the parties reached the following agreement. 2. The subject matter of this transfer refers to Zhongding Company's rights to the principal of 9 loans owed by Guizhou Company in the amounts of RMB 114,187,454.22 and USD 5,386,034.31, as well as interest, liquidated damages, etc., and the rights to the corresponding guarantors and collateral. 3. The total transfer price for the above debts is RMB 75 million. Taibao Company's payment schedule: (1) Within 46 days from the signing of this agreement, pay 20% of the total price as a deposit of RMB 15 million for the transferred debts, of which RMB 3 million shall be paid as a partial deposit on the date of signing the agreement; (2) Pay RMB 15 million as debt transfer payment to Zhongding Company by March 15, 2003; (3) Pay RMB 22.5 million as debt transfer payment to Zhongding Company by May 15, 2003; (4) Pay RMB 22.5 million as debt transfer payment to Zhongding Company by July 27, 2003; (5) For each of the above payment deadlines (including but not limited to the deposit), if Taibao Company has genuine difficulties in meeting the deadline, Zhongding Company grants Taibao Company a grace period of 60 days. (6) The account for payment: China Oriental Asset Management Corporation Guangzhou Office. 4. Regarding the transfer of debt documents: After this agreement takes effect, Zhongding Company agrees to transfer all debt documents under this agreement to Taibao Company within five working days after Taibao Company satisfies any one of the following two conditions, and to provide Taibao Company with a valid receipt of the transfer notice sent to the debtor and guarantor (if any) or other evidence proving that notice has been given: (1) Taibao Company pays the full transfer price of RMB 75 million to Zhongding Company by July 27, 2003, in accordance with this agreement; (2) Taibao Company pays the deposit of RMB 15 million to Zhongding Company in accordance with this agreement and provides Zhongding Company with a bank guarantee acceptable to Zhongding Company, ensuring that Taibao Company will pay the remaining RMB 60 million transfer price by July 27, 2003, in accordance with the above clause 2. 5. After this agreement takes effect, Zhongding Company allows Taibao Company to review and copy the relevant contracts, correspondence documents, bills, vouchers, and other debt documents under the transferred subject matter. 6. Regarding liability for breach of contract: (1) If either party violates any provision of this agreement, the other party has the right to demand immediate correction within a specified period; if the breach causes serious harm to the rights and interests of the other party, the other party has the right to rescind the agreement; (2) If Taibao Company pays the full transfer price on time and in full, the deposit paid by Taibao Company shall be offset against the transfer price; if Taibao Company fails to pay the transfer price on time within the payment period specified in this contract and the delay exceeds 60 days, Taibao Company shall be deemed in breach of contract, Zhongding Company has the right to rescind the agreement, and the deposit paid by Taibao Company shall not be refunded; for other transfer payments already made by Taibao Company in addition to the deposit, Zhongding Company shall offset them against the debts already transferred to Taibao Company in proportion to the total transfer price and total transferred debts, and Zhongding Company shall not require Taibao Company to return the transferred debts; for the portion offset, Taibao Company has no right to require Zhongding Company to refund the transfer price received; (3) If Taibao Company delays payment of the transfer price, it shall pay late fees to Zhongding Company for each day of delay in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China on overdue repayment; (4) If Zhongding Company fails to transfer the debts to Taibao Company after receiving the transfer payment, Zhongding Company shall refund the transfer payment already paid by Taibao Company, pay late fees in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China on overdue repayment, return twice the deposit, and compensate Taibao Company for all losses (including attorney fees and other expenses incurred and to be incurred by Taibao Company in realizing its claims); (5) If Zhongding Company delays transferring the debts to Taibao Company, Zhongding Company shall pay late fees in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China on overdue repayment; if such delay causes the debt to exceed the statute of limitations within three months after the transfer, it shall be handled in accordance with clause 4 of Article 5 (Zhongding Company's Responsibility) of this agreement; (6) In addition, the breaching party shall compensate the non-breaching party for losses caused by the breach or rescission of the agreement. 7. Regarding dispute resolution: All disputes arising from this agreement shall be resolved in accordance with the laws of the People's Republic of China and shall be under the jurisdiction of the court where Zhongding Company is located. 8. Regarding the effectiveness of the agreement: The agreement shall take effect upon being signed by the legal representatives or their authorized representatives and affixed with the official seals of both parties.

After the signing of this agreement, Taibao Company paid RMB 3 million on January 29, 2003; RMB 12 million on March 15; RMB 15 million on May 19; and RMB 9 million and RMB 14.5 million on September 19, totaling RMB 52.5 million in debt transfer payments to Zhongding Company.

On September 24, 2003, Zhongding Company issued a "Consent Letter" to Taibao Company, agreeing to extend the third installment of the transfer payment to 2003, with RMB 8 million to be paid on September 26 and RMB 14.5 million on September 29, and after receiving the third installment, agreed to pay the fourth installment by December 27, 2003. On the same day, Taibao Company also issued a "Consent Letter" to Zhongding Company, agreeing to transfer all debt documents to Taibao Company within 30 working days after Zhongding Company receives the full transfer price. On February 5, 2004, the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office sent a "Notice of Debt Transfer and Pledge" to the debtor Guizhou Company and the guarantors Guizhou Economic Development Corporation and Guizhou Town Investment Holding Corporation by notarial service. The Oriental Company Guangzhou Office and Zhongding Company jointly notified Guizhou Company, Guizhou Economic Development Corporation, and Guizhou Town Investment Holding Corporation that the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office had transferred all of its debt of RMB 158,773,046.24 against Guizhou Company to Zhongding Company, and that Zhongding Company had pledged the subject debts, including the above debt, as collateral to the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office. From the date of receipt of this notice, the debtor and guarantors should repay the debt to the new creditor in accordance with the instructions of the new creditor.

On February 6, 2004, Zhongding Company sent by mail to Taibao Company a "Notice Regarding the Transfer of the Debt of Guizhou Construction Comprehensive Development Company of Shunde City," stating: Based on Taibao Company's failure to pay the fourth installment, constituting a breach of contract, Zhongding Company hereby notifies the rescission of the "Debt Transfer Agreement," confiscates the deposit of RMB 15 million already paid, and does not refund the other transfer payments of RMB 37.5 million already paid. In accordance with clause 2 of Article 6 of the "Debt Transfer Agreement," Zhongding Company transfers the debt with a principal balance of RMB 79,487,454.22 in proportion to the payment already made against the total price. On the same day, Zhongding Company sent by mail to the debtor Guizhou Company a "Letter Regarding the Transfer and Handling of the Debt," notifying Guizhou Company that it had transferred the debt with a principal balance of RMB 79,487,454.22 and corresponding interest to Taibao Company. From the date of receipt of this notice, Taibao Company holds a claim over three loans under the above debt against Guizhou Company, and Zhongding Company retains the claim over other debts of Guizhou Company. On the same day, Zhongding Company also sent by mail to the guarantors Guizhou Economic Development Corporation and Guizhou Town Investment Holding Corporation a "Notice of Transfer of Security Rights."

On February 13, 2004, Zhongding Company delivered a "File Transfer List" to Taibao Company by notarial service, but Taibao Company refused to accept it.

On April 16, 2004, the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office issued a "Notice Regarding the Collection of the Price for the Shunde Asset Package" to Guangzhou Wanfang Xingtai Enterprise Consulting Co., Ltd., stating: As of January 6, 2004, Zhongding Company had paid the full price of RMB 318,622,497.7 for the Shunde asset package to the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office. On April 30, 2004, the Oriental Company Guangzhou Office issued a "Confirmation Letter Regarding the Retransfer of the Debt of Guizhou Construction Comprehensive Development Company of Shunde City" to Zhongding Company, stating: 1. Pursuant to the relevant agreements signed by your company and our office, your company has acquired from our office the above debt owed by Guizhou Company; since your company had satisfied all conditions precedent for acquiring the debt, your company had replaced our office as the creditor of Guizhou Company as of January 28, 2003, and held the above debt. 2. Pursuant to the relevant agreements signed by your company and our office, our office had a preemptive right to purchase the above debt transfer under the same conditions, but our office waived such preemptive right at that time. 3. Our office consents to the disposal plan for your company's above debt against Guizhou Company, i.e., transferring it to Taibao Company at a price of RMB 75 million and other conditions. 4. Our office agrees to release the pledge guarantee over such debts upon the transfer of the above debts, and shall no longer have a pledge right over such debts, and our office will assist your company in transferring the above debts to Taibao Company.

Additional Facts Found at First Instance: On January 24, 2003, Taibao Company and Ronggui District Investment Holding General Company entered into a "Historical Debt Settlement Agreement," stipulating: In view of the fact that the district-owned enterprises of Shunde City Ronggui District owed bank loans, and later the banks assigned part of the creditor's rights to China Orient Asset Management Corporation, China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, and China Cinda Asset Management Corporation, the total principal and interest of the creditor's rights held by the asset management corporations amounted to RMB 580,610,663.51, of which the principal and interest held by China Orient Asset Management Corporation totaled RMB 318,040,959.6. Taibao Company "packaged" and accepted the aforementioned creditor's rights of the three asset management corporations, reaching the following settlement plan: 1. Taibao Company agreed that for the creditor's rights of RMB 580.6 million, interest of RMB 275 million would be waived, and the amount would be calculated as RMB 305.6 million for collection. 2. Ronggui District Investment Holding General Company agreed to use 183,000 square meters of "Motor City" land at the original agreement price of RMB 800/square meter to offset the debt of RMB 146.4 million to Taibao Company. 3. Use 7,000 square meters of land on Wenhai Road to offset the debt of RMB 7 million to Taibao Company according to the original agreement. 4. Ronggui District Investment Holding General Company shall repay RMB 3 million to Taibao Company from the proceeds of disposing the factory building and land of Jinli Battery Factory. 5. After deducting the amount offset or paid to Taibao Company by Ronggui District Investment Holding General Company using the above land and partial payments from the principal creditor's rights of RMB 305,689,738.19, Taibao Company's remaining creditor's rights would be RMB 149,289,738.19. Taibao Company agreed to further waive RMB 49,289,738.19, leaving the remaining creditor's rights of Taibao Company at RMB 100 million. 6. If Taibao Company succeeded to the creditor's rights of loan principal of RMB 40,902,542.89 and derivative interest of Bank of China Shunde Sub-branch in Guizhou Construction Comprehensive Development Company, then Ronggui Subdistrict Office would pay an additional RMB 28 million to Taibao Company. If Taibao Company failed to succeed to the said loan principal and interest of Bank of China in Guizhou Construction Comprehensive Development Company, then with respect to the RMB 100 million to be paid to Taibao Company under Article 5 above, Taibao Company agreed to waive another RMB 20 million, meaning Ronggui District Investment Holding General Company would only pay RMB 80 million to Taibao Company. Etc.

On March 8, 2004, Taibao Company filed a lawsuit with the Guangdong High People's Court, requesting a judgment: 1. Declaring the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Taibao Company on January 29, 2003, to be an invalid contract. 2. Ordering Zhongding Company to return the transfer payment of RMB 37.5 million already paid by Taibao Company, to double refund the deposit totaling RMB 30 million, to compensate Taibao Company for lost profits of RMB 58.328 million, and for interest losses of RMB 1,911,818.22 (provisionally calculated based on the bank's same-period loan interest rate until February 29, 2004). The above items total RMB 127,739,818.22. 3. Ordering Zhongding Company to bear the costs of this case. During the trial of this case at first instance, the court of first instance did not recognize Taibao Company's claim regarding the validity of the civil act in this case, and pursuant to Article 35 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," informed Taibao Company that it could amend its claims. Accordingly, Taibao Company submitted a "Request for Amendment of Claims" to the court of first instance, changing the first claim to: Cancel the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Taibao Company on January 29, 2003.

The Guangdong High People's Court, after trial, held: This case is a dispute over a contract for debt transfer. The focus of the dispute is whether Zhongding Company's conduct constituted fraud, leading to the voidability of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed with Taibao Company.

Regarding whether Zhongding Company had already acquired the debt in question at the time of signing the "Debt Transfer Agreement" with Taibao Company. According to the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office on November 25, 2002, the intended transferred debt was to be transferred from Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office to Zhongding Company upon satisfaction of the preconditions stipulated in that agreement. On the same day the agreement was signed, Zhongding Company signed the "Management Service Provider and Fund Account Supervision Agreement," "Debt Pledge Contract," "Joint and Several Liability Guarantee Contract," "Service and Assistance Agreement," and "Preemptive Right and Repurchase Option Agreement" which were the stipulated preconditions, and paid the first installment of the transfer price to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office. At that point, Zhongding Company had satisfied the preconditions of the agreement, and the debt in question was transferred from Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office to Zhongding Company. Taibao Company's assertion that Zhongding Company had not acquired the debt in question at the time of signing the "Debt Transfer Agreement" with it is inconsistent with the facts.

Regarding the issue of Dongfang Company Office's preemptive right to purchase the debt in question. Although the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office stipulated that Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office had a preemptive right to purchase the debt upon its retransfer, Zhongding Company, prior to transferring the debt to Taibao Company, issued a notice of preemptive purchase to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office. Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office did not exercise that right within the period specified in Zhongding Company's notice, which should be deemed as a waiver of its preemptive right. In this regard, Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office also confirmed in a confirmation letter dated April 30, 2004, that it had waived its preemptive right at that time. Therefore, the impediment to Zhongding Company's transfer of the debt had been removed, and Zhongding Company could legally retransfer the debt it held.

Regarding whether the performance of the obligation to notify the debtor of the debt transfer affects the validity of the debt transfer agreement.

Article 80, paragraph 1 of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "If a creditor assigns its rights, it shall notify the debtor. Without such notification, the assignment shall not be effective against the debtor." Accordingly, if the creditor fails to notify the debtor, the assignment is not effective against the debtor, but it does not affect the validity of the debt transfer itself. Article 6, paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving the Acquisition, Management, and Disposal of Non-performing Loans of State-owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies" provides: "During the trial of a case, if the debtor argues on the ground that the original creditor bank failed to perform the notification obligation when assigning the debt, the people's court may summon the original creditor bank to court to investigate the facts of the debt transfer and order the original creditor bank to inform the debtor of the fact of the debt transfer." It can be seen that the obligation to notify the debtor of the debt transfer can still be performed during the trial, and the failure to perform the notification obligation in a timely manner only gives the debtor a right to defend against the assignee; it does not affect the validity of the debt transfer agreement between the assignor and the assignee. Therefore, issuing a notice of debt transfer to the debtor is not a condition for the validity of the debt transfer agreement. Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office's failure to notify the debtor and guarantor in a timely manner does not affect the validity of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" it signed with Zhongding Company, nor can it be concluded that Zhongding Company did not acquire the debt in question.

Regarding whether the pledge right held by Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office over the debt in question affects the validity of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Taibao Company. The "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office stipulated that Zhongding Company would pledge the acquired debt to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office as security for the repayment of the transfer price. However, in a letter dated April 30, 2004, Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office confirmed that it "released the pledge guarantee on the said debt at the time of the debt transfer and no longer holds a pledge right over the said debt." Therefore, Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office retroactively confirmed that it waived its pledge right when Zhongding Company transferred the debt in question to Taibao Company and does not have a pledge right over Zhongding Company's transfer of the debt in question. Even if, at the time Zhongding Company and Taibao Company signed the "Debt Transfer Agreement," Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office's pledge right over the transferred debt still existed, Zhongding Company could still transfer the debt. This is because the "Security Law of the People's Republic of China" does not prohibit the pledgor from transferring the pledged property. Even for objects such as stocks where the pledgee does not take possession of the pledged property, the law provides that they may be transferred with the consent of both the pledgor and the pledgee after negotiation. In this case, the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office both stipulated the pledge of the debt and also included provisions for the retransfer of the debt. Therefore, both parties actually agreed that the pledged debt could be retransferred. When Zhongding Company issued a "Notice of Preemptive Purchase" to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office in January 2003, intending to transfer the debt in question to Taibao Company, Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office did not raise any objection to the transfer. Therefore, the pledgee, Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office, had implicitly consented to the retransfer of the subject debt by the pledgor, Zhongding Company. Hence, Zhongding Company had the right to transfer the debt in question, and the validity of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" it signed with Taibao Company is not affected by the pledge of the debt.

Regarding whether Zhongding Company's conduct constituted fraud, making the "Debt Transfer Agreement" voidable. Article 68 of the Supreme People's Court's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "If one party intentionally informs the other party of a false situation, or intentionally conceals the true situation, inducing the other party to make a false declaration of intent, it may be deemed as fraudulent conduct." In this case, the preamble of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Taibao Company states: "Pursuant to the 'Debt Transfer Agreement' signed between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office on November 25, 2002, Zhongding Company has acquired the relevant debts in the Shunde area and the security rights under those debts transferred from Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office to Bank of China. The parties have negotiated and reached this agreement in accordance with the rules and procedures agreed with Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office and obtaining legal recognition." It can be seen that at the time of signing the debt transfer agreement in this case, Taibao Company should have been aware of the content of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office and had an understanding of the situation of the debt in question. Therefore, Taibao Company's claim that Zhongding Company intentionally concealed the content of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" it signed with Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office, inducing it to make a false declaration of intent and thus sign the "Debt Transfer Agreement" in this case, lacks factual basis. With respect to the conditions set for the retransfer of the debt in the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office, the declarations and warranties required from the new proposed assignee mainly include acknowledging the legal personality of Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office as an enterprise legal person, understanding and recognizing that Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office does not hold any form of claim against the People's Republic of China and its government based on the original subject debt, etc. These contents do not constitute the so-called substantial restrictions and constraints on Taibao Company's recovery of the debt in question. As for the fact that Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office had not yet notified the debtor and guarantor of the debt transfer at the time Zhongding Company and Taibao Company signed the transfer agreement, and the fact that Zhongding Company had pledged the subject debt to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office, as discussed above, these do not affect Zhongding Company's acquisition of the debt in question from Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office, nor do they affect the validity of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Taibao Company. Although Taibao Company might be temporarily hindered in asserting the debt against the debtor because the notice of debt transfer had not reached the debtor and the debt was pledged, according to the facts of this case, the debt transfer agreement signed between Zhongding Company and Taibao Company stipulated that only after Taibao Company paid the full transfer price would Zhongding Company deliver to Taibao Company the materials for all debts under the agreement and issue to the debtor and guarantor valid receipts for the transfer notice or other evidentiary materials proving that notice had been given. However, at the time Taibao Company initiated this lawsuit, it had not yet paid the full transfer price, and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office had already performed the obligation of notifying the guarantor of the debtor in this case of the debt transfer on February 5, 2004. Regarding the issue of the pledge, Zhongding Company had paid the full consideration for the Shunde asset package to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office on January 6, 2004. Since the pledge right is extinguished when the secured claim is extinguished, Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office's pledge right was automatically extinguished on January 6, 2004. Therefore, by the time Taibao Company had not yet acquired the debt in question, the obligation to notify the debt transfer, which would affect Taibao Company's ability to exercise rights against the debtor, had been performed, and the pledge right had also been extinguished, causing no harm to Taibao Company's interests. Taibao Company's request to cancel the "Debt Transfer Agreement" does not meet the requirements of Article 54, paragraph 2 of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China" and is not supported. Furthermore, according to Article 55 of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," if a party with the right to cancel fails to exercise that right within one year from the date it knew or should have known of the grounds for cancellation, the right to cancel shall be extinguished. Since at the time of signing the "Debt Transfer Agreement" in this case, Taibao Company should have known about the content of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office; and Article 3, paragraph 1 of the parties' agreement also stipulates: "After this agreement takes effect, Zhongding Company allows Taibao Company to inspect and copy the relevant contracts, correspondence documents, bills, vouchers, and other debt materials under the subject debt," meaning that after signing the agreement, Taibao Company had the right to know the situation of the debt. Therefore, Taibao Company should have known about the grounds for its claimed cancellation at the time of signing the agreement on January 29, 2003. By the time it filed this lawsuit on March 8, 2004, more than one year had passed. Therefore, Taibao Company's argument that Zhongding Company's conduct constituted fraud and that the agreement was voidable lacks sufficient grounds and is not supported.

In summary, the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Taibao Company does not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and administrative regulations and should be deemed lawful and valid. Zhongding Company's conduct did not constitute fraud. Taibao Company's claim that the agreement is voidable, and its request for Zhongding Company to return the paid debt transfer price and compensate for interest losses, lack factual and legal basis. Taibao Company's request for Zhongding Company to double refund the deposit and compensate for lost profits is inconsistent with the legal consequences of claiming the agreement is voidable. Taibao Company's claims are not supported. The court, pursuant to Article 44, paragraph 1, Article 54, paragraph 2, Article 55, and Article 80, paragraph 1 of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," and Article 64, paragraph 1 of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," adjudicated: Dismiss all of Taibao Company's claims. The case acceptance fee of RMB 648,709 shall be borne by Taibao Company.

Taibao Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing: (1) The judgment of first instance found that Zhongding Company had acquired the debt in question at the time of signing the "Debt Transfer Agreement" with Taibao Company, which is inconsistent with the facts. Because Zhongding Company did not notify the debtor Guizhou Company and the guarantors Guizhou Economic Development General Company and Guizhou Town Investment Holding General Company until February 5, 2004, that it had provided the subject debt, including the debt in question, as a pledge to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office. Only then were the preconditions for the debt transfer stipulated in the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office satisfied, proving that at the time of signing the "Debt Transfer Agreement" with Taibao Company, Zhongding Company had not acquired the debt in question. Therefore, the judgment of first instance confused two different issues: the validity of the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office and Zhongding Company, and the performance of that agreement. (2) The judgment of first instance's finding that Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office had waived its pledge right is inconsistent with the facts. Its finding that Zhongding Company could still transfer the debt after pledging it to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office is illogical in legal principle and avoids the core issue of whether Zhongding Company concealed from Taibao Company the fact that the debt in question had been pledged at the time of signing the contract, i.e., whether it informed Taibao Company of the pledge to enable Taibao Company to make a correct decision. The so-called retroactive confirmation in Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office's letter of April 30, 2004, not only occurred after the commencement of this lawsuit but also contradicts the fact that it sent a notification letter to the borrower and guarantor on February 5, 2004. (3) The judgment of first instance's finding that Zhongding Company did not conceal the true situation of the debt at the time of signing the contract with Taibao Company is erroneous. There are two key issues in this case: first, whether at the time of signing the "Debt Transfer Agreement," Zhongding Company had acquired the creditor's rights for the loan principal and corresponding interest involved in this case, as it claimed; second, whether it informed Taibao Company of the fact that the debt had been pledged. At the time of signing the "Debt Transfer Agreement," Zhongding Company had not acquired the relevant debt, its relevant statements were false, and it did not inform Taibao Company of the fact that the debt was pledged. Therefore, Zhongding Company clearly intentionally concealed, constituting fraud. (4) Regarding the limitation period. At first instance, there was no evidence that Taibao Company knew that Zhongding Company had not acquired the debt in question at the time of signing the agreement on January 29, 2003, nor was there evidence that Taibao Company knew at the time of signing that Zhongding Company had pledged the relevant debt to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office. Moreover, because the "Debt Transfer Agreement" between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office contained billions of other debts unrelated to this case, and due to various confidentiality agreements between Zhongding Company and Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office, Zhongding Company, citing confidentiality, had consistently refused to provide relevant documents, Taibao Company could not have known the above facts. Taibao Company learned that the precondition for Zhongding Company to acquire the debt was after the exchange of evidence before the trial of this case, and learned the time when Zhongding Company had pledged the relevant debt to Dongfang Company Guangzhou Office was after February 5, 2004. Therefore, Taibao Company's initiation of this lawsuit on March 8, 2004, did not exceed the one-year period. (5) The trial procedure of first instance did not comply with regulations. During the first instance proceedings, because the court did not recognize Taibao Company's claims, it informed Taibao Company that it could amend its claims. Taibao Company submitted a "Request for Amendment of Claims" to the court. Pursuant to Article 35 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," the court should have designated a new period for the submission of evidence, but the court of first instance did not designate a period as required by law, and furthermore, did not conduct a trial hearing on the amended claims, which does not comply with legal provisions. Taibao Company requests that the original judgment be reversed according to law, and that the "Debt Transfer Agreement" signed between the parties on January 29, 2003, be cancelled, and that Zhongding Company be ordered to return the transfer payment of RMB 37.5 million already paid by Taibao Company, to double refund the deposit totaling RMB 30 million, and to compensate Taibao Company for lost profits and interest losses.

Appellee Zhongding Company argued in its defense as follows: (1) The subject claim in dispute in this case has been transferred from the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company to Zhongding Company, and Zhongding Company has the right to further transfer the claim it acquired from the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company to Taibao Company. According to the terms of the "Claim Transfer Agreement" signed between Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company, on the date of signing the agreement, Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company signed the various contracts stipulated as conditions precedent and paid the first installment to the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company in accordance with the agreement. Zhongding Company had fulfilled the conditions precedent stipulated in the "Claim Transfer Agreement", and the subject claim was transferred to Zhongding Company. The facts show that at the time of signing the "Claim Transfer Agreement" with Taibao Company, Zhongding Company had already lawfully and effectively acquired the subject claim. Given that the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company had waived its right of first refusal, Zhongding Company's transfer of the subject claim to Taibao Company did not violate any laws or regulations. Moreover, the "Claim Transfer Agreement" represented the true intention of both parties and was lawful and valid. After the parties signed the "Claim Transfer Agreement", Taibao Company paid part of the claim transfer price to Zhongding Company, but Taibao Company failed to pay the fourth installment on the agreed date, constituting a breach of contract. Zhongding Company rescinded the "Claim Transfer Agreement" in accordance with the agreement. (2) Taibao Company argued that the conditions precedent stipulated in the "Claim Transfer Agreement" between Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company were not satisfied, and that Zhongding Company had not yet acquired the claim at the time of signing the "Claim Transfer Agreement" with Taibao Company, on the grounds that Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company had not issued a notice to the borrower and the guarantor regarding the pledge of the subject claim to the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company. This ground of appeal is untenable. The absence of a notice of claim assignment does not affect the validity of the claim assignment between the assignor and the assignee; it merely grants the debtor a defense right against the assignee. The existence of such a defense right does not mean that the assignee has not validly acquired the claim; it only means that the exercise of the claim is temporarily hindered, and this defense right is extinguished once the notice of claim assignment reaches the debtor. Since issuing a notice to the debtor is not a condition for the validity of the claim assignment, the determination of when the assignee replaces the assignor as the creditor should be based on the agreement between the assignor and the assignee, not on the time when the notice is issued to the debtor. Therefore, when Zhongding Company acquired the claim should be determined based on the terms of the "Claim Transfer Agreement" signed with the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company and the content of the letter from the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company dated April 30, 2004. (3) Taibao Company's grounds of appeal, that the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company's waiver of the pledge right was inconsistent with the facts, that the transfer of a claim after a pledge is legally impermissible, and that the issue of the claim pledge was evaded, are without any factual or legal basis. From the confirmation letter issued by the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company on April 30, 2004, it can be determined that the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company discharged the pledge at the time Zhongding Company and Taibao Company signed the "Claim Transfer Agreement" to transfer the claim. This expression of intent to discharge the pledge was made before Zhongding Company and Taibao Company signed the "Claim Transfer Agreement" and became effective at the time of signing the agreement. The confirmation letter was merely a subsequent written confirmation and does not mean that the expression of intent to discharge the pledge was made on April 30, 2004. At the same time as Zhongding Company notified Taibao Company of the rescission of the "Claim Transfer Agreement" signed between them, Zhongding Company notified the debtor of the matter of transferring the relevant claim to Taibao Company. It can be seen from this notice that there was no content regarding a claim pledge, and therefore no claim pledge existed. (4) Based on the foregoing facts that Zhongding Company had lawfully acquired the claim and, at the time of signing the "Claim Transfer Agreement", Taibao Company should have known and did know the content of the agreement between Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company, it can be determined that Zhongding Company neither intentionally informed Taibao Company of false information nor intentionally concealed the true situation. Therefore, Zhongding Company did not commit fraud, and Taibao Company does not have the right to rescind. Even if Taibao Company had the right to rescind, that right has been extinguished due to the expiration of the statute of limitations. According to the rules of evidence, if Taibao Company claims that it did not know the grounds for rescission as of January 29, 2003, it should provide corresponding evidence to prove this. The evidence Zhongding Company submitted to prove that Taibao Company should have known and did know the grounds for rescission at the time of signing the contract is the "Claim Transfer Agreement" signed by both parties. Taibao Company also failed to provide any evidence to rebut Zhongding Company's claim. Therefore, Taibao Company's argument that the statute of limitations had not expired cannot stand. (5) The trial procedure of the first instance was correct. During the first instance, Taibao Company changed its claim from seeking confirmation of the invalidity of the "Claim Transfer Agreement" to rescission. Pursuant to Article 2, paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings", Taibao Company should provide corresponding evidence for the changed claim. However, the evidence Taibao Company relied upon to seek confirmation of the invalidity of the "Claim Transfer Agreement" was exactly the same as the evidence relied upon to seek rescission of the "Claim Transfer Agreement". Regarding the evidence Taibao Company relied upon to seek confirmation of the invalidity of the "Claim Transfer Agreement", the court of first instance had designated a period for submitting evidence and conducted a pre-trial exchange of evidence in accordance with relevant regulations. Where Taibao Company changed its claim but did not provide different evidence, it was entirely proper for the court of first instance not to separately designate a new period for submitting evidence. Therefore, the trial procedure of the first instance was correct. (6) Taibao Company's request for Zhongding Company to return the transfer price already paid and pay double the deposit, and to compensate for its lost profit and interest losses, is without legal and factual basis. The "Claim Transfer Agreement" in this case represented the true intention of both parties and was legally binding on both. However, Taibao Company did not pay the transfer price on time as agreed in the "Claim Transfer Agreement". Zhongding Company had the right to rescind the agreement and retain the transfer price already collected, while simultaneously transferring the corresponding proportion of the claim to Taibao Company. Zhongding Company has completed the transfer of the corresponding proportion of the claim. Therefore, Taibao Company is not entitled to demand the return of the transfer price from Zhongding Company. Furthermore, due to Taibao Company's breach of contract, it is not entitled to demand the return of the deposit, and this claim contradicts Taibao Company's litigation request. In summary, Taibao Company's appeal should be dismissed.

This Court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

This Court holds that the focus of the dispute between the parties in this second instance remains whether Zhongding Company held the claim at the time of signing the contract, whether the pledge between Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company affected the retransfer of the claim, and whether Zhongding Company's conduct constituted fraud.

Regarding Taibao Company's ground of appeal that Zhongding Company did not acquire the claim in this case at the time of signing the contract, this Court holds that the main basis for Taibao Company's ground of appeal is that Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company failed to issue a notice regarding the pledge of the subject claim to the borrower and the guarantor in accordance with the terms of the "Claim Transfer Agreement" signed between them, and thus the conditions for the agreement to take effect were not satisfied. According to the facts found in this case, on the same day Zhongding Company signed the "Claim Transfer Agreement" with the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company, the parties also signed the "Management Service Provider and Fund Account Supervision Agreement", "Claim Pledge Contract", "Joint Liability Guarantee Contract", "Service and Assistance Agreement", and "Right of First Refusal and Repurchase Option Agreement" stipulated as conditions precedent. Thereafter, Zhongding Company paid the first installment transfer price of RMB 165,683,698.8 in accordance with the agreement. The above facts show that the main conditions for the agreement to take effect, as agreed by the parties, had been satisfied. Although Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company failed to promptly issue a notice regarding the pledge of the subject claim to the borrower and the guarantor, based on the content of the "Notice of Claim Transfer and Pledge" subsequently issued by the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company, the prerequisite for the claim pledge was that the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company transferred the subject claim to Zhongding Company, and Zhongding Company provided the subject claim as collateral to the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company. It can be seen that the obligation to notify of the claim pledge agreed upon in the agreement between Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company has the same legal significance as the obligation to notify of the claim transfer. Therefore, the court of first instance correctly held that issuing a notice of claim transfer to the debtor is not a condition for the validity of a claim transfer agreement, and the failure of the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company to timely issue a notice of claim transfer to the debtor and the guarantor does not affect the validity of the "Claim Transfer Agreement" signed with Zhongding Company, nor can it be concluded that Zhongding Company did not acquire the claim in this case. The above determination in the judgment of first instance is correct, and Taibao Company's ground of appeal cannot stand and is not adopted by this Court. Regarding Taibao Company's ground of appeal that the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company did not waive the pledge right and the subject claim was non-transferable, this Court holds that the main basis for Taibao Company's ground of appeal is that in the notice letter dated February 5, 2004, issued by the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company to the borrower and the guarantor, it was expressly stated that the subject claim had been pledged, and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company also asserted the pledge right against the borrower and the guarantor. Therefore, the so-called waiver of the pledge right in the letter from the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company dated April 30, 2004 is inconsistent with the facts. The facts found in this case show that the "Notice of Claim Transfer and Pledge" issued by the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company to the borrower and the guarantor was merely a notification to the borrower and the guarantor regarding the claim pledge, and it cannot be concluded that the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company was asserting the pledge right against the borrower and the guarantor. The "Claim Transfer Agreement" between Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company contained clauses regarding the claim pledge and the retransfer of the claim, with the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company having the right of first refusal regarding the retransfer of the claim. The claim Zhongding Company transferred to Taibao Company was only part of the claim it had acquired from the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company. Before Zhongding Company transferred this part of the claim to Taibao Company, it issued a "Notice of Right of First Refusal" to the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company. The Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company did not exercise its right of first refusal within the agreed period and did not object to Zhongding Company's transfer of this part of the claim to Taibao Company. This transfer did not violate the parties' agreement or any mandatory provisions of laws or regulations. Moreover, in its letter dated April 30, 2004, the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company confirmed the fact that "upon the transfer of the above-mentioned claim, the pledge guarantee for such claim was discharged, and it no longer holds a pledge right over such claim." Therefore, the court of first instance correctly held that the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company had waived the pledge right regarding Zhongding Company's transfer of this part of the claim, that Zhongding Company had the right to transfer the claim in this case, and that the validity of the "Claim Transfer Agreement" signed with Taibao Company was not affected by the pledge of the claim. The above determination in the judgment of first instance is correct, and Taibao Company's ground of appeal cannot stand and is not adopted by this Court.

Regarding Taibao Company's ground of appeal that Zhongding Company concealed the true situation of the claim, constituting fraud, this Court holds that, based on the analysis above, at the time Zhongding Company signed the "Claim Transfer Agreement" with Taibao Company, it had already acquired the subject claim from the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company. Taibao Company's assertion that the time of issuance of the notice of claim pledge is the time when Zhongding Company acquired the relevant claim, and its claim that the related statements in the "Claim Transfer Agreement" signed with Taibao Company were false and constituted concealment of the true situation of the claim, are without factual and legal basis. When Taibao Company signed the "Claim Transfer Agreement" with Zhongding Company, it was clear that the agreement was reached based on the "Claim Transfer Agreement" between Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company, and was lawfully recognized in accordance with the rules and procedures agreed upon by Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company. It should be determined that Taibao Company was aware of the content of the agreement between Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company at the time of signing, and it did not object to Zhongding Company's pledge of the acquired subject claim to the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company. If Taibao Company claims that it was not aware of the content of the agreement between Zhongding Company and the Guangzhou Office of Dongfang Company at the time of signing, this can only be regarded as Taibao Company's waiver of its own rights, and does not prove that Zhongding Company intentionally concealed the fact that the claim had been pledged. Therefore, Taibao Company's ground of appeal that Zhongding Company's conduct constituted fraud is without factual basis and is not supported by this Court.

Regarding Taibao Company's claim that after it submitted the "Application for Amending Litigation Claims" to the court of first instance, the court of first instance did not re-designate a period for submitting evidence in accordance with Article 35 of the "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings", nor did it hold a hearing for the amended litigation claims, this Court holds that after the first instance trial, Taibao Company submitted an application for amending litigation claims to the court of first instance. Thereafter, the court of first instance notified Taibao Company that it could amend its litigation claims and clearly informed Taibao Company that if it did so, it needed to submit a written application and relevant evidence. Within the specified period, Taibao Company submitted the application for amending litigation claims to the court of first instance but did not provide relevant evidence. Furthermore, during the second instance trial, Taibao Company also did not provide this Court with evidence related to its amended litigation claims. Therefore, Taibao Company's claim cannot stand.

In summary, Taibao Company's grounds of appeal are without factual and legal basis. The judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law, and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 648,709 shall be borne by Foshan Shunde Taibao Investment Management Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
